elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "... and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate" for commercial general liability.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "where MSL processes any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for IBM, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" — the trigger covers every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Customer rather than selected named data types.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "MSL shall provide certificates of insurance to IBM on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O of not less than USD 2,000,000 exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability of not less than USD 5,000,000 exceeds the USD 2,000,000 floor; the condition ("where MSL processes any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for IBM") is broad and applies here, since MSL holds access to IBM I/T systems and data.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Not required at the fallback level, but in any event expressly included in the inserted clause.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: the only insurance obligations in the document are asset-specific (replacement-value cover on consigned Products at §13.1 and joint-insured status on IBM-owned tooling at §21.2), with no CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' compensation or certificate right anywhere.

All six preferred elements are satisfied by a single concise insertion in the General article; the deterministic gates (operation applies, insurance obligation present, element coverage) are confirmed on the operative text, not merely mechanically.
The cyber trigger is drafted to reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Customer, so it does not fail the named-data-type restriction.

Minimality holds: for a missing clause a concise insertion of wholly new words is acceptable, and the drafter stripped the model-language extras ("at its own expense" and the one-year survival tail), added no procedures, notice mechanics, additional-insured, waiver-of-subrogation, or rating requirements, and left the existing consigned-Product and tooling insurance sentences untouched.

Intent is preserved: the new clause sits alongside rather than displacing §13.1 and §21.2, creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict the retained freight/shipment insurance cost allocations.
The margin comment correctly states the preferred position and offers the fallback (E&O USD 1,000,000 / cyber USD 2,000,000) without relying on the comment to supply any operative term.
